item.title: 🎯 First they cleared the skies, then – the strongholds Servicemen of the Sever Group of Forces told about the fighting for the settlement of
item.description: First they cleared the skies, then – the strongholds Servicemen of the Sever Group of Forces told about the fighting for the settlement of Annopolye in Kharkov region. 🎯 Before assaulting, the servicemen cleared the skies of enemy strike drones. Then artillery and UAV teams struck the positions of an AFU separate motorised infantry brigade and destroyed strongholds, firing points and field ammunition depots. ▫️ Assaultmen of the 128th Motorised Rifle Brigade (44th Army Corps) advanced through forest areas in poor visibility, supported by tube and rocket artillery. The fighters operated in small groups of two or three, while reconnaissance UAV operators adjusted their actions from the air. Task completed! Moving on 💪 🔹 Russian Defence Ministry

item.content:encoded:
Original source: https://t.me/mod_russia_en/29995

The Armed Forces of the Russian Federation continue the special military operation.
⚡️
Units of the Sever Group of Forces in Kharkov region
continue to tighten the encirclement and expand the external control zone.
🔥
Fights are underway in the encirclement for the liberation
of Nikolayevka, Varvarovka, Nefedovka, and Chernoye (Kharkov region).
▪️
The AFU lost over 55 troops, a motor vehicle, and five ground-based robotic systems in the encirclement ring during the day.
📍
Russian troops expand the external control zone. Russian elements continue combat actions to establish control over the settlements of Prikolotnoye, Kotovka, and Gogino (Kharkov region).
💥
In addition, in Kharkov region
, manpower and hardware of two mechanised brigades, one motorised infantry brigade, one assault regiment of the AFU, and one territorial defence brigade have been hit near Svetlichnoye, Slatino, Martovoye, Shirokoye, Bugaevka, and Velikiy Burluk (Kharkov region).
🔥
In Sumy region, strikes were delivered
at formations of two mechanised brigades of the AFU and three territorial defence brigades close to Yuryevo, Barilovka, Radkovka, Velikaya Rybitsa, and Olshanka (Sumy region).
▪️
In total, the enemy lost more than 295 troops, an armoured personnel carrier, two armoured fighting vehicles, eight motor vehicles, and one field artillery gun in the Sever Group's area of responsibility.
↗️
The Zapad Group's units improved the situation along the front line and inflicted losses
on manpower and hardware of two mechanised assault brigades, one assault brigade of the AFU, and one territorial defence brigade near Volchiy Yar, Berezovka, Blagodatovka, Tamarganovka, Osinovo, Maleyevka, and Grushevka (Kharkov region).
▪️
The AFU losses amounted to up to 220 troops, two armoured fighting vehicles, nine motor vehicles, and two electronic warfare stations.
📍
The Yuzhnaya Group of Forces took more advantageous lines and positions.
Strikes were delivered at formations of two mechanised brigades, one mountain assault brigade, one unmanned systems brigade of the AFU, and one marine brigade close to Yasnogorka, Belenkoye, Nikolayevka, Vasilevskaya Pustosh, Druzhkovka, Semenovka, Kramatorsk, and Slavyansk (Donetsk People's Republic).
▪️
The enemy lost up to 195 troops, one armoured fighting vehicle, 23 motor vehicles, two artillery guns, and one electronic warfare station.
👉

🔹
Russian Defence Ministry

item.title: ➡️ Teaching combat drones to win smarter: Russian MoD launches AI training service for military purposes
item.description: Teaching combat drones to win smarter: Russian MoD launches AI training service for military purposes The Ministry of Defence of the Russian Federation has created a service providing developers of unmanned systems with access to objective control data from the combat employment of drones, aimed at training military-purpose neural networks. ➡️ The new service provides developers of unmanned systems with access to a specialised storage facility offering prepared video footage showing the employment of FPV drones , as well as other copters and fixed-wing UAVs. 'More than 40 organisations involved in training neural networks, including for integration into their own combat unmanned systems, are currently connected to the service,' noted Russian Deputy Defence Minister Dmitriy Shcherbinin, under whose leadership the project is being implemented. ✅ Specialists of the Russian Ministry of Defence have also created a unified data recognition classifier for AI machine learning , allowing developers to work with the dataset efficiently, in a structured manner and according to a common concept. 📄 The results of the work by military unmanned systems developers are uploaded back into the service , where the information is checked for completeness and compliance with the classifier format, allowing the Russian Ministry of Defence to use this dataset to create and train its own neural networks. 📈 This approach makes it possible to enhance the resilience and adaptability of the Armed Forces
item.content:encoded:
Original source: https://t.me/mod_russia_en/29984

Teaching combat drones to win smarter:
Russian MoD launches AI training service for military purposes
The Ministry of Defence of the Russian Federation has created a service providing developers of unmanned systems with access to objective control data from the combat employment of drones, aimed at training military-purpose neural networks.
➡️
The new service provides developers of unmanned systems with access to a specialised
storage facility offering prepared video footage showing the employment of FPV drones
, as well as other copters and fixed-wing UAVs.
'More than 40 organisations involved in training neural networks, including for integration into their own combat unmanned systems, are currently connected to the service,' noted Russian Deputy Defence Minister Dmitriy Shcherbinin, under whose leadership the project is being implemented.
✅
Specialists of the Russian Ministry of Defence have also
created a unified data recognition classifier for AI machine learning
, allowing developers to work with the dataset efficiently, in a structured manner and according to a common concept.
📄
The results of the work by military unmanned systems developers are uploaded back into the service
, where the information is checked for completeness and compliance with the classifier format, allowing the Russian Ministry of Defence to use this dataset to create and train its own neural networks.
📈
This approach makes it possible to enhance the
resilience and adaptability of the Armed Forces of the Russian Federation to modern challenges
in the field of artificial intelligence.
🔒
The service is provided with information security
based on certified information protection tools using modern cryptography and authentication means.
🔹
Russian Defence Ministry
